title: Polynomial classical space, linear quantum space: exact-gate arbitrary-modulus Regev pairing sieve

claims.statement: For every integer N>=2 and every fixed s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N). The single polynomial-space dyadic pairing algorithm with arbitrary-modulus projection reduction in proof.md recovers the entire s with unconditional success probability at least2/3 from independent ideal mixed coset copies. For n>=2 its fixed parameters are P=2^m with m=floor(log2 N), b=ceil(sqrt(n log2 n)), A=16(b+4)/15, D=ceil((m-1)/b), V=ceil(100 n^2 A^D), R=ceil(20000V), q=ceil(log2(100R)), decoder precision q_label=ceil(log2(100RV)), at mostV recursive node starts and at most200V original source acquisitions per trial, and at mostR trials. Each combination of width w uses w+4 inputs. For n=1 test each candidate in order with seven fresh copies per candidate as specified in proof.md. On every execution branch the total charged sequential work is T=O(n^10 2^(2 n^(1/2)(log2 n)^(1/2)+(5/2)n^(1/2))). This includes bit operations, circuit generation, addressing, exact Clifford+T gates, measurements, initialization, all projections and retries, source charges, and every failed trial. This is its complete representative bit-length envelope; its exact growth index is1/2. All constants are absolute and these four resource guarantees hold jointly for this same configuration and success guarantee.
